entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Urius emerges from the historical record as an Alemannic petty king during the tumultuous mid-4th century CE, a period defined by intensifying Roman-Germanic frontier conflicts. His significance lies not in individual military prowess or expansive rule, but as one of several tribal leaders whose collective actions and subsequent diplomatic engagement with the Roman Emperor Julian profoundly shaped the immediate stability of the Rhine frontier. His participation in the peace treaty of 359 CE, alongside other prominent Alemannic kings, underscores the complex and often fluid power dynamics between the declining Western Roman Empire and the ascendant Germanic confederations at its borders. Urius represents the localized, yet cumulatively impactful, challenge to Roman authority that characterized Late Antiquity.

The pivotal event involving Urius occurred in 359 CE, when the future Emperor Julian, then Caesar of Gaul, launched a decisive campaign across the Rhine. Following Roman military successes, Julian initiated negotiations at Mogontiacum (modern Mainz). The contemporary historian Ammianus Marcellinus meticulously records that Julian compelled a peace treaty from a coalition of Alemannic kings, including Urius, Hariobaudes, Macrian, Vadomarius, Ursicinus, and Vestralpus. This treaty, secured through a combination of Roman military pressure and diplomatic acumen, aimed to stabilize the frontier, ensure the return of Roman captives, and potentially impose a tributary status on the Alemannic tribes, at least temporarily.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Urius, as one of the Alemannic kings involved in the 359 CE peace treaty with Emperor Julian, played a specific role in a pivotal moment of Roman frontier history. His actions contributed to the temporary stabilization of the Rhine frontier, directly impacting Roman efforts to secure Gaul against Germanic incursions.
